text: Meanwhile, a rival was growing. Pepsi-Cola was born in North Carolina in 1898, and it went bankrupt more than once.
In those hard years, Coca-Cola reportedly had chances to buy Pepsi. It passed every time.
Pepsi fought back with price. During the Great Depression, it sold a twelve-ounce bottle for a nickel. The same price as Coke's six-and-a-half-ounce bottle.
Coke answered with feelings. In 1971, it filmed young people from around the world on a hilltop in Italy, singing about buying the world a Coke. A version of that song became a hit on the radio.
Pepsi answered with taste. In the Pepsi Challenge, which started in 1975, people took a sip from two unmarked cups... and on camera, a lot of them picked Pepsi.
Coke was still bigger, but it was losing ground. And inside the company, someone asked a dangerous question: what if we change the taste?
